svg.title: Base Revenue to $217,150 Owner Profit
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-03-base-owner-profit-waterfall; chart type: waterfall; title: Base Revenue to $217,150 Owner Profit; subtitle: $505,000 less $287,850 modeled expenses equals a 43.0% net margin; chapter number: 3; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Formula v2.0 Base revenue, margin, and owner profit are canonical. The four expense allocations are illustrative because the supplied scorecard does not itemize costs. First and last bars are totals; the intervening bars are negative changes. Gross means gross operator fee revenue, not gross client refund receipts.; caption: Reconciliation: $505,000 - $145,000 - $40,850 - $60,000 - $42,000 = $217,150; $217,150 / $505,000 = 43.0%. Conservative remains $110,000 at 30% = $33,000; Scaled remains $900,000 at 56% = $504,000.; stages: label: Earned operator fee revenue; value: $505,000 annual Base revenue; numeric value: 505000.0; detail: Include earned contingency shares, earned portions of 36-month shared-savings agreements, and completed WOTC processing fees. Apply ASC 606 principal-agent analysis to the actual arrangement; client benefits are never automatically operator billings.; label: Pod delivery labor; value: Subtract $145,000 allocated annual labor; numeric value: -145000.0; detail: Illustratively allocate $145,000 to employee compensation and contractor delivery across the 1 FT plus 3 C pod. The resulting owner-profit figure is the residual after this modeled labor charge, not a separate estimate of owner compensation.; label: Variable case execution; value: Subtract $40,850 case-linked operating costs; numeric value: -40850.0; detail: Illustratively allocate case-specific records, permitted filing charges, incremental extraction services, and recovery processing costs here. Exclude contractor labor already charged to the preceding bar to prevent double counting.; label: Commercial and administrative overhead; value: Subtract $60,000 annual commercial overhead; numeric value: -60000.0; detail: Illustratively allocate acquisition, insurance, bookkeeping, and general administration to a $5,000 monthly fixed-cost budget. Track acquisition cost per signed engagement rather than per unqualified lead.; label: Platform and secure operations; value: Subtract $42,000 annual platform overhead; numeric value: -42000.0; detail: Illustratively allocate $3,500 monthly to OCR, permitted integrations, secure storage, access management, and monitoring. Combined fixed overhead is $8,500 monthly, within the stated $1,500-$9,500 range; this allocation excludes the delivery and variable costs shown separately.; label: Annual owner net profit; value: $217,150 retained annual operating residual; numeric value: 217150.0; detail: The endpoint is a total, not another additive movement. Total modeled expenses are $287,850, leaving exactly 43.0% of Base operator revenue. Owner-level personal taxes and distribution timing are outside this supplied scenario.

circle.title: label: Earned operator fee revenue; value: $505,000 annual Base revenue; numeric value: 505000.0; detail: Include earned contingency shares, earned portions of 36-month shared-savings agreements, and completed WOTC processing fees. Apply ASC 606 principal-agent analysis to the actual arrangement; client benefits are never automatically operator billings.

label: Pod delivery labor; value: Subtract $145,000 allocated annual labor; numeric value: -145000.0; detail: Illustratively allocate $145,000 to employee compensation and contractor delivery across the 1 FT plus 3 C pod. The resulting owner-profit figure is the residual after this modeled labor charge, not a separate estimate of owner compensation.

label: Variable case execution; value: Subtract $40,850 case-linked operating costs; numeric value: -40850.0; detail: Illustratively allocate case-specific records, permitted filing charges, incremental extraction services, and recovery processing costs here. Exclude contractor labor already charged to the preceding bar to prevent double counting.

label: Commercial and administrative overhead; value: Subtract $60,000 annual commercial overhead; numeric value: -60000.0; detail: Illustratively allocate acquisition, insurance, bookkeeping, and general administration to a $5,000 monthly fixed-cost budget. Track acquisition cost per signed engagement rather than per unqualified lead.

label: Platform and secure operations; value: Subtract $42,000 annual platform overhead; numeric value: -42000.0; detail: Illustratively allocate $3,500 monthly to OCR, permitted integrations, secure storage, access management, and monitoring. Combined fixed overhead is $8,500 monthly, within the stated $1,500-$9,500 range; this allocation excludes the delivery and variable costs shown separately.

label: Annual owner net profit; value: $217,150 retained annual operating residual; numeric value: 217150.0; detail: The endpoint is a total, not another additive movement. Total modeled expenses are $287,850, leaving exactly 43.0% of Base operator revenue. Owner-level personal taxes and distribution timing are outside this supplied scenario.

text.title: Assumptions: Formula v2.0 Base revenue, margin, and owner profit are canonical. The four expense allocations are illustrative because the supplied scorecard does not itemize costs. First and last bars are totals; the intervening bars are negative changes. Gross means gross operator fee revenue, not gross client refund receipts.
